summary: 11 of the 12 per-model chat-completions commands (all Gemini/Claude chat variants; grok_responses.go is the sole exception with proper SSE handling) must (a) default --stream to false and (b) reject an explicit --stream=true with a clear error instead of attempting to decode the SSE response through the generic JSON path. A reprint that regenerates these files without both parts reintroduces default-invocation breakage (a) and silent malformed/base64-garbled output on explicit --stream (b).
reason: Kie.ai's chat-completions endpoints for these models document stream:true as their own API default, and the spec faithfully carried that default into the generated CLI flag. But only grok_responses.go's generated body sends the Accept: text/event-stream + X-Printing-Press-Text-Response header pair and decodes the resulting text envelope; the other 11 commands POST through the plain JSON response path. Flipping the flag default to false fixes the common case; a caller who still explicitly passes --stream would otherwise hit the same broken decode path, so that case is now rejected up front with an explanatory error rather than left to fail unpredictably. Replicating grok_responses.go's SSE-envelope handling into these 11 more complex commands (each with its own partial-failure detection, human-table rendering, and --compact/--select filtering) was judged too risky to do blind without a real API key to verify the decode against live streamed output -- the guard is the honest interim fix.
validated_outcome: go build ./... and go vet ./... pass. Manually verified against the live API for gemini-2-5-flash: `--stream` alone returns a clean guard error (exit 1); default invocation (no --stream) reaches api.kie.ai and gets back a real, cleanly-decoded JSON error body (401 unauthorized, expected with a placeholder credential) rather than a decode failure; `--dry-run --stream` correctly bypasses the guard to preview the request. The other 10 files share the identical generated shape and guard placement but were only build/vet-verified, not live-called individually.
